title: The Weather Week
subtitle: Ilma Kask's six-week system for training, light and sauna through an Estonian winter
promise: Six weeks to a training week that survives a six-hour day.

sections.title: A letter from Ilma
paragraphs: Every November I used to disappear. Not dramatically. The runs just got shorter, then optional, then a thing I would definitely start again on Monday.
Everyone thinks their November is the worst one. It is not a character flaw. It is a plan built for eighteen hours of light, used in a month that gives you about six.
This book is the plan I built for the short days: one board, four kinds of work, and six weeks to make the week hold.

sections.title: Why this works
paragraphs: Adults are generally advised to get **150 to 300 minutes** of moderate activity a week. Spread across a week you can actually keep, that is less than it sounds.
Morning daylight, regular sleep timing and a warm-then-cool sauna habit are ordinary routines with a long tradition in the north. This guide treats them as habits, not treatments.
*This is not medical advice.* If something hurts sharply, stop and ask a professional.

sections.title: Week 3 · The Wobble
sections.rule: Shrink the session, never the week.
paragraphs: Week three is when the novelty is gone and the dark is not. Nothing gets harder this week. Two things get shorter. The board stays.
**Place of the week:** the Nõmme to Harku health trails in Tallinn. The five-kilometre loop is lit all night.

sections.title: The honest small print
paragraphs: Ilma Kask is an AI-generated character. The places are real; the routines are ordinary habits, not medical advice.
If you are struggling, talk to someone. In Estonia: emotional support line 116 123 (daily 10:00 to 24:00), family doctor advice line 1220 (24/7), emergencies 112.
